stewart_read: Textbook 'hello objection' in the first 30 seconds; rep doesn't run the small-ask template verbatim but achieves the same function by pivoting to the existing scheduled estimate.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep ignored the objection entirely and got lucky the customer kept talking.
coaching_implication: Works here because the customer kept volunteering info, but rep should have an explicit small-ask ready ('30 seconds to explain why I'm calling') for when the customer doesn't self-resume.

quote: I had a few guys come by with Iron Solar before, and and they told me how my house is positioned directly in sunlight

quote: So it is kinda perfect for solar panels, but I ain't really liked about it yet.

coaching_implication: Rep could have mirrored this ('sounds like your roof is a great fit') to build curiosity heading into the appointment; instead it passed without acknowledgment.

quote: I'm kinda sold on it, but I ain't convinced her yet.

coaching_implication: Good execution — worth using as a positive exemplar per schema's note on this exact call (SESSION18_fd078269).

quote: I mean, once I get her in advance, there'll be no problem.

quote: hopefully, we can be able to, get your wife on board too once she's able to, you know, understand it a little more.
stewart_read: Third touch, at button-up — reinforces intent but never gets an explicit yes that she'll be on the appointment.
coaching_implication: Should have asked directly: 'Will she be able to join us for that call?' to convert intent into a confirmed co-owner attendance.

quote: well, that's what this meeting is for is to kinda explain to you guys both how it works

alternative_hypothesis: Could also be read as legitimate booking rationale, not true scope creep, since no product specifics were given.
coaching_implication: Low-severity; keep language to 'the specialist will walk you both through the numbers' rather than implying the rep will cover benefits.
